transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-11
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Evan Brooks, Priya Shah, Miguel Ortega (Redwood) — Mark Rivers, Laila Chen, Samir Patel, Dana Ito (Pyxis Logistics)

Summary: quick fidelity/quality scan of current POC runs; focus on scoring drift, prompt-level failure modes, guardrail false positives, and plan for a targeted benchmark with quantized model variants. Next steps: share eval spreadsheet, run quantized bench, customer to provide extra edge-case prompts and VPC/network details.

Topics:
- Recent scorecard drop on Return-to-Sender prompts
- Guardrail false alarms impacting throughput
- Latency/cost trade for int4 vs int8 on dedicated instances
- Data isolation and VPC peering questions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan: ok great hi everyone thanks for jumping on, let's do a quick round of where we are — we ran the stability sweep last week and bumped into a few new failure clusters, i want to get aligned on root cause and a short remediation runway
[00:18] Mark: yeah thanks Evan, we saw the scorecard drop from 93 to about 87 on the last nightly — most of the diffs are on the return-to-sender and multi-leg routing prompts, seems like hallucination-ish but sometimes the model just omits a carrier id, so downstream validation flags it
[00:35] Priya: mmhm, we pulled the failed examples — many are short context prompts where prior shipment state is implicit. The model seems to prefer brevity and drops the explicit carrier tag, which trips our parser. Some of those are also affected by a prompt template change earlier this sprint
[00:50] Laila: i should have flagged that prompt tweak — product asked to shorten user-facing copy; looks like we didn't test the reduced context with the post-processing parser
[01:05] Miguel: quick question on scoring, are we seeing this only on the hosted variant or across dedicated as well?
[01:12] Dana: both, but more pronounced on the hosted runs where we tried the 'fast' variant, which uses a trimmed context window — so it correlates with sequence length and context truncation
[01:30] Priya: ok so two axes: prompt-template regression (human change) and model/config variant (fast vs baseline). We should separate those in the eval to attribute cause. I'd propose a delta table that slices by prompt template, model variant, and sequence length bucket
[01:50] Samir: also worth noting we saw guardrail false positives on four examples where the model used a phrase like "not qualified" and the safety filter flagged it — that caused an automatic fallback and raised latency by 300-400ms for those requests
[02:08] Evan: i remember that — the fallback policy's conservative rules are catching safe-but-ambiguous phrasing. Can we show an example?
[02:16] Samir: sure, example here: "Customer instructed to hold two pallets, not qualified for expedited review" — the safety regex interpreted "not qualified" as a refusal/negative content and triggered blocking
[02:30] Priya: that smells like a false positive from the guardrail classifier threshold; we can retune the threshold or add exception rules for shipment domain tokens like "expedited" or "pallet"
[02:45] Laila: but we can't loosen too much because we have enterprise compliance that forbids certain content transits — also SOC2 audit is coming up and we need a clear audit trail of guardrail decisions
[03:00] Evan: absolutely, we can keep strict logging but tune the runtime threshold so it doesn't fallback for these shipping-specific phrasings. We'll log the reason code and sample on any changed threshold for auditability
[03:15] Mark: on the audit trail, do you capture the full prompt + model response or just hashes? we have some compliance rules about PII persistence
[03:26] Miguel: standard Redwood practice is to offer configurable retention, by default we redact PII and store redacted transcripts — for Private deployments you can route logs to customer-controlled KMS and retain as you like. We'll send the SOC2 appendix that outlines retention modes
[03:44] Evan: noted, action item for me to share that doc after the call.
[03:50] Dana: jumping back to evaluation — our scoring function weights exact-match on carrier id very high. Could that be amplifying small formatting diffs into big score drops?
[04:03] Priya: yes, exact-match makes sense for strict downstream validation but it's brittle to punctuation and whitespace changes. We recommend a fuzzy normalization step: canonicalize carrier ids before scoring, and run a secondary semantic-match score for the rest of the payload
[04:22] Samir: would the normalization be client-side pre- or post-model? we prefer client-side to avoid model retraining
[04:30] Priya: normalization is typically post-processing in the eval harness — we can supply a normalization script you can run on both golden and candidate outputs so the metric is fair
[04:40] Laila: sounds good. also curious about quantized model runs you mentioned earlier — what's the latency/cost delta you're seeing?
[04:50] Priya: high level: int8 gives ~30% token-cost reduction with a 10-15% latency bump on our dedicated pools; int4 can be 55-65% cost reduction but latency variance increases and some fidelity regressions appear on long-context examples. The trade is workload-dependent — for short, structured prompts int4 often works, for long multi-turn contextual prompts int8 or baseline float is safer
[05:15] Mark: interesting — our production-ish pipeline mixes short validation calls and longer plan-generation calls. Can we run split routing so validation uses int4 and plan-gen uses higher-fidelity model?
[05:27] Evan: yes, Redwood supports policy-based routing. You can route by route name, token budget, or latency SLO. We can show an example policy and a canary rollout for split traffic
[05:40] Laila: is that a hard requirement to use Dedicated for quantized runs?
[05:46] Priya: not strictly — hosted can also expose quantized variants but with allocation limits; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and more control over kernel selection which matters at high QPS
[05:58] Samir: on dedicated, what about autoscale? we need to avoid cold-start latency spikes during morning batch windows
[06:06] Evan: Dedicated has configurable autoscale policies and warm pools, and you can pre-provision burst capacity. We'll show our recommended policy for your QPS profile in the benchmark doc
[06:20] Mark: ok, about the failure clustering — can Redwood produce a heatmap that groups failure modes by prompt template and failure reason? that would speed triage
[06:30] Miguel: yes, the Eval dashboard supports failure tagging and heatmaps. We can export a CSV first while we onboard you to the dashboard. We'll include per-prompt examples and failure reason codes
[06:44] Dana: one more item, we saw a run where the KV cache seemed to not populate and subsequent completions repeated system context, which messed up the slot filling — could that be a runtime bug?
[06:56] Priya: we did see an edge-case in our continuous batching code where under certain packetization the K-V cache index shift happens for >8k context windows — it's rare but reproducible. We pushed a patch to the staging cluster; we'll run the same inputs from your failing batch to validate
[07:14] Samir: awesome — would you need the exact request logs for that?
[07:19] Priya: yes if you can share those (redacted for PII) that would help. Samir mentioned VPC peering earlier — if we can run the test in your dev VPC it shortens the repro loop
[07:32] Samir: ok i'll follow up with peering details as an action item.
[07:37] Laila: switching to guardrails again — could we get a per-rule impact report? like which guardrail rules triggered most and false-positive rate?
[07:46] Miguel: we can provide a per-rule breakdown, including counts and an example sample for each rule. We'll also include the timeline of triggers so you can correlate with cadence and prompt changes
[07:58] Mark: for the upcoming SOC2, we need a compact package: logs/retention, access controls, RBAC mapping, and key management notes — can Redwood produce that as a one-pager?
[08:10] Evan: yes we'll produce a SOC2 appendix one-pager plus the full compliance bundle. I'll attach links in the follow-up email.
[08:18] Dana: about the eval spreadsheet — can the scoring include a new column for "failure type" (parsing, hallucination, guardrail, formatting)? that will help triage owners
[08:29] Priya: absolutely — we'll add a failure_type column and a normalized_text column after applying the canonicalizer. Also we'll add a confidence score so you can threshold for manual review
[08:40] Laila: small ask — can Redwood run a gated experiment to compare our current prompt template vs the shortened one, but only on 10% of traffic to measure real-world delta?
[08:51] Evan: yes, we can do a canary split 10/90 and capture the scorecard delta, as well as micro-metrics like parse success and guardrail hits. We'll script it so it's reversible within an hour
[09:05] Mark: what's the expected timeline for the quantized benchmark you proposed?
[09:10] Priya: i can run the first pass on Monday with our infra; end-to-end we'll need sample set + labeling from you. If we get the 2k prompts by Tuesday, bench complete by Thursday; results + spreadsheet by Friday
[09:24] Samir: concerning networking — will peered tests show identical latency as customer-on-prem? our infra has some egress NAT that adds jitter
[09:32] Miguel: peered tests are good for functional repro but absolute latency numbers will differ from on-prem. We'll include a note and also run a synthetic test that simulates your NAT jitter profile so the numbers are comparable
[09:47] Laila: any concerns about exposing raw prompts to Redwood for the eval? we have some restricted PII in a subset of examples
[09:57] Evan: we can accept redacted prompts; alternatively we support in-VPC eval where the data never leaves your VPC and Redwood runs the eval in your private plane. We'll include both options in the follow-up
[10:14] Dana: thanks — i prefer the in-VPC run for the 2k edge cases but can send redacted versions for the initial triage
[10:24] Priya: noted; we'll plan for in-VPC for the formal bench. We'll also prepare an initial quick-run on the redacted set to surface the biggest clusters
[10:36] Mark: i want to flag procurement cadence — procurement is evaluating Dedicated, but finance needs cost numbers for int4/int8 routing options for a 12-month commit
[10:48] Evan: we'll produce a delta cost model spreadsheet showing per-token costs, estimated monthly spend at your QPS, and incremental savings from caching+batching options. That will help finance with scenarios
[11:02] Laila: ok great, sounds like we have a plan. can we recap next steps quickly?
[11:08] Evan: recap — Evan to share SOC2 appendix and security snapshot; Priya to run quantized bench once Dana provides prompts; Priya/Miguel to produce per-rule guardrail impact and heatmap; Samir to share VPC peering/firewall details; Dana to upload 2k edge-case prompts (redacted or in-VPC). Schedule benchmark run for 2027-05-20 10:00 PT.
[11:33] Mark: cool, thanks team. we'll aim to have the prompts and peering details by the dates we discussed.
[11:38] Evan: awesome, thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet and links. bye

End of transcript.
